self_assessment: Added db.sortedSetIncrByBulk(data) taking an array of [key, increment, value] tuples and returning the resulting scores in input order, to all three backends. Redis queues one zincrby per tuple on a multi and runs it through the existing helpers.execBatch, mapping each reply through parseFloat. Postgres reuses module.sortedSetIncrBy via Promise.all so the increments run concurrently and the results stay positional. Mongo builds an unordered bulk op of upserting $inc updates on { _key, value }, executes it, then re-reads the affected docs (projected to _key/value/score) and maps them back to the input order by key:value; lodash was added to that file for the _.uniq on the query. Verified by extracting the three implementations into a scratch script and running them against in-memory fakes of the redis multi, mongo bulk/find and postgres single-increment APIs: existing members, brand-new key-member pairs, several ops on one set, repeated ops on one member and negative increments all produce the expected ordered scores. Note the one behavioural difference this design implies: for two increments of the same member in one call, redis and postgres report the intermediate then final score (1, 3) while mongo reports the final score twice (3, 3), since it re-queries after the bulk - that follows from each backend's natural batching primitive. NodeBB's own suite could not be run here since it needs a live redis/mongo/postgres plus a built asset bundle; node --check passes on all three files.
